method: COMPILED FROM 2 SOURCES. S1: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand 'Discoid lupus erythematosus' (2022), 16 claims; LICENCE: © DermNet. Website terms cl. 11: all information on the site is protected by copyright; cl. 14: reproduction for other purposes needs DermNet's written permission (read at https://dermnetnz.org/terms (read 2026-09-23)). S2: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762) 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update' (published online 12 October 2023), 9 claims; LICENCE: © Author(s) (or their employer(s)) 2024. No commercial re-use. See rights and permissions. Published by BMJ. (read at copyright line on page 1 of the published PDF (University of Szeged repository copy of the BMJ version)). Verify each source separately: verify.py --source <file> --only-source S<n>. Source text: the DermNet topic page fetched with urllib/curl, scripts, styles and navigation removed, tags stripped. Edition 2.0 adds S2, the EULAR 2023 SLE recommendations (published BMJ PDF from the University of Szeged repository, pdftotext, zero-width characters and soft hyphens removed), paraphrased; the S1 claims are unchanged.

claims.claim: **Discoid lupus (DLE) is a chronic, scarring skin disease and the commonest cutaneous lupus.** Long-lasting scaly plaques, mainly on the face, scalp and ears, can leave scars, atrophy, pigment change and permanent hair loss.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **It mostly affects women in their 20s to 40s** and is rare in children. It is commoner in skin of colour; New Zealand data show a markedly higher relative risk for Māori and Pacific peoples than for people of European descent.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **UV light can provoke DLE,** though lesions also occur on covered skin. Smoking is commoner in people with DLE and makes antimalarials work less well.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **DLE is localised above the neck in 80% and generalised in 20%.** Early red patches become plaques with adherent scale and follicular plugs (the 'carpet-tack' sign when scale is lifted), with favourite sites being the nose, cheeks, ear lobes and the conchal bowl of the ear.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Some develop SLE:** about 5% with localised DLE and 15% with generalised DLE.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine fully for other signs of lupus,** and confirm with a skin biopsy in most cases.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Baseline tests:** full blood count, renal function, ANA (often negative) and urinalysis.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Differentials include** lichen planus, actinic keratosis, polymorphic light eruption, drug-induced and chilblain lupus, squamous cell carcinoma, sarcoidosis and lupus vulgaris.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Protect from the sun all year, with clothing plus generous high-SPF broad-spectrum sunscreen;** sunscreen on its own is not enough. Some people need to avoid window glass indoors or fit UV-blocking film.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Recommend vitamin D supplements for people who strictly avoid the sun, and help them stop smoking.**
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First treatment for localised DLE: intermittent courses of potent or ultrapotent topical corticosteroid for several weeks.** Intralesional corticosteroid injection is sometimes used.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Topical calcineurin inhibitors** (tacrolimus ointment, pimecrolimus cream) are an alternative.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Camouflage make-up and wigs** help confidence when scarring is extensive.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Oral prednisone or prednisolone** can give short-term control.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Longer-term systemic options, alone or combined,** include hydroxychloroquine, chloroquine, mepacrine, methotrexate, acitretin or isotretinoin, mycophenolate, dapsone, thalidomide and biologics (belimumab, rituximab), among others.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Skin disease in SLE, first line:** a topical steroid or calcineurin inhibitor, an antimalarial, and a systemic steroid if needed. **Second line:** anifrolumab, belimumab, methotrexate or mycophenolate.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Hydroxychloroquine for every patient with SLE unless contraindicated, aiming at 5 mg/kg of real body weight a day,** with the dose tailored to that person's risks of flare and of retinal toxicity.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Closer eye follow-up for those at higher retinal risk:** kidney disease, existing macular or retinal disease, or tamoxifen.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **In moderate or severe disease a higher starting dose (above 5 mg/kg/day, never over 400 mg/day) is allowed,** coming back into range once the patient improves.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Where it is available, a hydroxychloroquine blood level can guide the dose and show poor adherence;** testing everyone routinely is not practical.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Chloroquine can stand in where hydroxychloroquine is unavailable, but is likely more toxic to the retina.** Mepacrine (quinacrine) can be added after an inadequate response, or replace hydroxychloroquine after retinopathy, though intolerance and poor availability limit it.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **About 40% do not respond to first-line treatment.** In one small retrospective series of 73 refractory patients, methotrexate and mycophenolate did about equally well (around 65%).
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Dapsone, retinoids, calcineurin inhibitors, azathioprine, cyclophosphamide and rituximab remain later options,** best chosen with a dermatologist experienced in CLE. ⚠️ Keep thalidomide and lenalidomide for disease that has failed several agents, with the greatest care in women who could become pregnant; lenalidomide carries less polyneuropathy risk.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Systemic steroids:** dose by organ and severity, bring them down to no more than 5 mg/day of prednisone (or equivalent) for maintenance, and stop them when possible.
claims.locator: EULAR task force (Fanouriakis A, Kostopoulou M, Andersen J, et al.), Annals of the Rheumatic Diseases 2024;83:15-29 (doi 10.1136/ard-2023-224762), 'EULAR recommendations for the management of systemic lupus erythematosus: 2023 update', published online 12 October 2023, http://publicatio.bibl.u-szeged.hu/28452/3/34193576_megjelent.pdf, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **DLE is chronic and can last for years; treatment is often difficult.** ⚠️ Squamous cell carcinoma can rarely develop in a long-standing plaque on skin or mucosa.
claims.locator: DermNet (Alani Z, Jarrett P; previous contributor Oakley A), New Zealand, 'Discoid lupus erythematosus', 2022, https://dermnetnz.org/topics/discoid-lupus-erythematosus, retrieved 2026-09-23
